t: The facility of the United States Postal Service located on Franklin Avenue in Pearl River, New York, shall be known and designated as the “Heinz Ahlmeyer, Jr. Post Office Building”.

fable.w: This section only names a postal facility; Congress makes the designation directly by statute. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge any federal decision, so there is nothing that crosses the federal boundary. There is no real tempting opposite reading, as the text contains no procedural or consultative language at all.
fable.s: shall be known and designated as the “Heinz Ahlmeyer, Jr. Post Office Building”.

opus.w: This section only names a Postal Service facility. It has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. Nothing in it is on-topic for participation, so the label is No.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply designates the name of a federal facility. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) in making this decision. The act of naming is a unilateral legislative action.
qwen_chat.s: The facility of the United States Postal Service located on Franklin Avenue in Pearl River, New York, shall be known and designated as the “Heinz Ahlmeyer, Jr. Post Office Building”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that naming a building after a person involves some form of public recognition or consultation, but the text itself contains no procedural requirement for outside parties to participate in the decision to name the building. It is a unilateral legislative designation.
